<description>
Seednodes are used for addr-fetch connections. When the network is disabled (`networkactive=0` or `setnetworkactive false`), the seednodes are consumed without ever being dialled and  When the network becomes active again, no further addr-fetch attempts are made, even though the seednodes are still configured. They remain unavailable until the node is restarted.

This happens because `ThreadOpenConnections()`, continues running its loop while the network is disabled. With < 2 outbound peers or an empty addrman, a seednode is popped from `seed_nodes` , queued as an addr-fetch, and then popped again from `m_addr_fetches` in `ProcessAddrFetch()`. It is then dropped because `OpenNetworkConnection()` returns early when the network is inactive. Once the network is re-enabled, no seednodes remain. Anchors were lost in the same way before #34213.

This change makes `ThreadOpenConnections` wait while the network is re-enabled, as the way `ThreadPrivateBroadcast` does, so no connection state is used up while the network is disabled
</description>

<commits>
405ea4a6a3 net: check network activity before attempting to create connections

ThreadOpenConnections kept running its loop while the network was inactive.
OpenNetworkConnection() refused every attempt, but by then the loop had
already popped seednodes and addr-fetch entries, which were then lost.

31129ec13e test: check that seednodes are kept while the network is inactive
</commits>
